examples.text: Света, слушай, я хочу кое-что сказать.
examples.trans: Sveta, listen, I want to tell you something.

examples.text: Слушай, ты мне что-то сказать хотел?
examples.trans: Listen, did you want to tell me something?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Поэтому мы должны всё честно рассказать.
examples.trans: Therefore we must tell everything honestly.

examples.text: Катя, а ты уже совсем готова?
examples.trans: Katya, are you completely ready already?

examples.text: Ну, в принципе, можно и пойти.
examples.trans: Well, in principle, we can go.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Слушай, а она мне не старовата?
examples.trans: Listen, is she not a bit too old for me?

examples.text: Она привезёт к нам одинокую подругу.
examples.trans: She will bring her single friend to our place.

examples.text: Она доцент.
examples.trans: She's a lecturer.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'allergy' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Кажется, у неё аллергия на лекарство!
examples.trans: It seems she has an allergy to the medicine!

examples.text: У меня аллергия на кошек.
examples.trans: I'm allergic to cats.

examples.text: У него аллергия на икру.
examples.trans: He's allergic to caviar.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам пора наконец перестать так прятаться.
examples.trans: It is time for us to finally stop hiding like this.

examples.text: А вы не пойдёте с нами?
examples.trans: Are you not coming with us?

examples.text: Пойдём, мы вас на улице подождём.
examples.trans: Let us go, we will wait for you outside.

meanings.note: From Latin 'doctor' (teacher, scholar, from 'docere', to teach).

examples.text: Доктор, помогите нам, пожалуйста, скорее!
examples.trans: Doctor, please help us quickly!

examples.text: Доктор, мне срочно нужен гипс.
examples.trans: Doctor, I urgently need a cast.

examples.text: Больно, больно! Очень больно, доктор!
examples.trans: It hurts, it hurts! It hurts very much, Doctor!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: А вы без моей помощи обойдётесь?
examples.trans: And will you manage without my help?

examples.text: Доктор, помогите нам, пожалуйста, скорее!
examples.trans: Doctor, please help us quickly!

examples.text: Я помогаю вам в последний раз.
examples.trans: I am helping you for the last time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Поэтому мы должны всё честно рассказать.
examples.trans: Therefore we must tell everything honestly.

examples.text: Денис, скорее, мы в кино опаздываем!
examples.trans: Denis, hurry, we are running late for the cinema!

examples.text: Пойдём, мы вас на улице подождём.
examples.trans: Let us go, we will wait for you outside.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корее').

examples.text: Денис, скорее, мы в кино опаздываем!
examples.trans: Denis, hurry, we are running late for the cinema!

examples.text: Скорее всего, вы про меня слышали.
examples.trans: Most likely, you have already heard about me.

examples.text: Никита, иди скорее вызывай сюда скорую!
examples.trans: Nikita, go quickly and call an ambulance here!

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, я сейчас.
examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.

examples.text: Подождите минуту.
examples.trans: Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Подождите, сейчас я внимательно её посмотрю.
examples.trans: Wait, I will examine her carefully right now.

examples.text: Очень интересно, я внимательно слушаю вас.
examples.trans: Very interesting, I am listening to you attentively.

examples.text: Читайте всё внимательно!
examples.trans: Read everything carefully!

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will look', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.text: Можно я посмотрю?
examples.trans: May I have a look?

examples.text: Я только посмотрел.
examples.trans: I only had a look.

examples.text: А можно я пойду посмотрю?
examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?
